MAUI Template Sample - Windows x64 TEST installer

1. Download the GitHub artifact ZIP and choose Extract All once.
   Keep the MSIX, public CER, scripts, install.json and Dependencies together.
2. On your Windows x64 PC, open Windows PowerShell as administrator USING YOUR
   OWN ACCOUNT, change directory to the extracted folder, and run:
       .\Install-WindowsTestApp.ps1
3. Review the publisher and certificate thumbprint. Only if you trust this
   download and your IT policy permits it, type TRUST when prompted.
4. Open "MAUI Template Sample" from Start.

The script installs the MSIX with Windows' Add-AppxPackage. The app includes its
.NET and Windows App SDK runtime files. Any required framework packages are
included in Dependencies and signature-checked; no separate SDK is needed.
The package's minimum Windows version is recorded in install.json. Windows 11
x64 is recommended. This package is not for ARM64-only or 32-bit Windows.

This is a self-signed TEST certificate, not a production Microsoft signature.
The one-time approval adds only that certificate to Local Computer >
Trusted People. NEVER install it into Trusted Root Certification Authorities.
The certificate is public-only; no private signing key or password is shipped.
A later build may use a different test certificate and require approval again.

An organization may block sideloading, unsigned PowerShell scripts or test
certificates. Ask IT if blocked; do not enable Developer Mode, change execution
policy, disable security tools or bypass your organization's restrictions.
If you cannot elevate your own account, ask IT to install the certificate into
LocalMachine\TrustedPeople and deploy the MSIX/dependencies to your user.
Double-clicking the MSIX alone does not establish certificate trust or ensure
framework dependencies are installed.

Uninstall normally from Windows Settings > Apps. To remove test publisher
trust afterward, remove only the thumbprint shown in install.json from
Local Computer > Trusted People (administrator/IT permission required).
No trust is silently added; cancellation before approval leaves trust unchanged.

provenance.json identifies the exact source-built MAUI framework and template
snapshot. validation.json records what CI actually verified, including whether
installation and launch succeeded; a successful package build alone is not
evidence that it ran on your PC or passed accessibility/screen-reader testing.
